title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to their safety-belt reminders
scope_summary: This Regulation approves vehicle types with regard to their safety-belt reminder (SBR) system, which detects unfastened safety-belts and alerts the driver through first and second level warnings. It applies to all seating positions fitted with a safety-belt in vehicles of categories M and N.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to all seating positions in vehicles of categories M and N fitted with safety belt with regard to safety-belt reminders.
applies_to_components: Detection of an unfastened safety-belt (buckle engagement or pulled-out webbing length)
Visual warning (lighting, blinking or visual display of symbol or message)
Ignition switch / vehicle master control switch activation logic
Safety-belt buckle and retractor as sensing points for unfastened status
relation_to_other_regulations: Created by splitting UN Regulation No. 16 into three regulations (GRSP 73rd session, May 2023): safety-belts and restraint systems (components), safety-belts and child restraint systems installation (vehicle), and safety-belt reminders (vehicle, this Regulation).
Requirements are derived from UN Regulation No. 16 as amended by the 09 series of amendments and are technically identical.
UN Regulation No. 16, 10 series of amendments, is to contain transitional provisions explaining equivalence between approvals under this Regulation and UN R16 09 series.
Definition of second level warning refers to paragraphs 8.4.2.4.1.1. to 8.4.2.4.1.3. (numbering carried over from UN R16).
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.7).
Application and approval numbering per Schedules 3 and 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other Regulations under which the vehicle is approved (para. 4.5).
Section 11.2 contains transitional provisions applicable to the 01 series of amendments.

defined_terms.label: Safety-belt reminder
defined_terms.definition: A system dedicated to alert the driver when any occupant does not use the safety-belt, constituted by detection of an unfastened belt and two levels of driver alert (first and second level warning).

defined_terms.label: Visual warning
defined_terms.definition: A warning by visual signal (lighting, blinking or visual display of symbol or message).

defined_terms.label: Audible warning
defined_terms.definition: A warning by sound signal.

defined_terms.label: First level warning
defined_terms.definition: A visual warning activated when the ignition switch or vehicle master control switch is activated and any occupant's safety-belt is not fastened, with an optional audible warning.

defined_terms.label: Second level warning
defined_terms.definition: A visual and audible warning activated when the vehicle is operated per paras 8.4.2.4.1.1. to 8.4.2.4.1.3. and the safety-belt is or becomes unfastened, depending on the seating position requirement.

defined_terms.label: Safety-belt is unfastened
defined_terms.definition: At the manufacturer's option, either the buckle of any occupant is not engaged or the pulled-out webbing length is less than needed to buckle an unoccupied rearmost seat.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle is in normal operation
defined_terms.definition: The vehicle is in forward motion at a speed greater than 10 km/h.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type with regard to its Safety-belt reminder
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in location of the visual warning, type of audible warning, first and second level warning strategy and maximum number of seating positions.

defined_terms.label: Safety-belt (seat-belt, belt)
defined_terms.definition: An arrangement of straps with buckle, adjusting devices and attachments anchored in a power-driven vehicle to reduce injury risk by limiting wearer mobility, including energy-absorbing or retracting devices (belt assembly).

defined_terms.label: Lap belt
defined_terms.definition: A two-point belt passing across the front of the wearer's pelvic region.

defined_terms.label: Diagonal belt
defined_terms.definition: A belt passing diagonally across the front of the chest from the hip to the opposite shoulder.

defined_terms.label: Three-point belt
defined_terms.definition: A belt essentially combining a lap strap and a diagonal strap.

defined_terms.label: S-type belt
defined_terms.definition: A belt arrangement other than a three-point belt or a lap belt.

defined_terms.label: Harness belt
defined_terms.definition: An S-type belt comprising a lap belt and shoulder straps, optionally with a crotch strap assembly.

defined_terms.label: Strap
defined_terms.definition: A flexible component designed to hold the body and transmit stresses to the belt anchorages.

defined_terms.label: Buckle
defined_terms.definition: A quick-release device enabling the wearer to be held by the belt, which may incorporate the adjusting device except for harness belt buckles.

defined_terms.label: Belt adjusting device
defined_terms.definition: A device enabling the belt to be adjusted to the wearer and seat position, possibly part of the buckle, retractor or other belt part.

defined_terms.label: Retractor
defined_terms.definition: A device to accommodate part or the whole of the strap of a safety-belt.

defined_terms.label: Seat
defined_terms.definition: A structure, integral or not with the vehicle, complete with trim, intended to seat one adult person, including an individual seat or part of a bench seat.

defined_terms.label: Front passenger seat
defined_terms.definition: Any seat whose foremost H-point is in or in front of the vertical transverse plane through the driver's R-point.

defined_terms.label: Forward-facing seat
defined_terms.definition: A seat usable in motion facing the front of the vehicle with its plane of symmetry within ±10° of the vehicle's.

defined_terms.label: Rearward-facing seat
defined_terms.definition: A seat usable in motion facing the rear of the vehicle with its plane of symmetry within ±10° of the vehicle's.

defined_terms.label: Side-facing seat
defined_terms.definition: A seat usable in motion facing the side of the vehicle at 90° (±10°) to the vehicle's plane of symmetry.

defined_terms.label: Group of seats
defined_terms.definition: Either a bench-type seat or separate side-by-side seats accommodating one or more seated adults.

defined_terms.label: Bench seat
defined_terms.definition: A structure complete with trim intended to seat more than one adult person.

defined_terms.label: Seat anchorage
defined_terms.definition: The system by which the seat assembly is secured to the vehicle structure, including the affected structure parts.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle master control switch
defined_terms.definition: The device bringing the vehicle's on-board electronics from switched-off to normal operation mode (ready to drive).

classes_and_variants.name: First level warning
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Visual warning (optional audible) at activation of ignition/master control switch when a belt is unfastened

classes_and_variants.name: Second level warning
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Visual and audible warning when vehicle is operated (e.g. normal operation >10 km/h) and a belt is or becomes unfastened

classes_and_variants.name: Unfastened detection by webbing length
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Manufacturer option: pulled-out webbing shorter than needed to buckle unoccupied rearmost seat

classes_and_variants.name: Driver seating position
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Specific requirements and test procedure (Annex 3 para. 2.1)

classes_and_variants.name: Front passenger seat
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Foremost H-point in or in front of the transverse plane through the driver's R-point

classes_and_variants.name: Rear / other seating positions
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Seating positions behind the front row, with position-specific requirements and exemptions (para. 5.1)

classes_and_variants.name: Forward-, rearward- and side-facing seats
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Seat orientation relative to the vehicle plane of symmetry

classes_and_variants.name: Belt types (lap, diagonal, three-point, S-type, harness)

applicability_hints: This is a whole-vehicle approval; components (buckle switches, seat occupancy sensors, telltales, chimes, instrument cluster/HMI software) are not approved separately but their behaviour determines compliance.

Applies to every seating position fitted with a safety-belt, not only the driver: rear seats, side-facing and rearward-facing seats and bench seats in M and N vehicles (subject to exemptions in 5.1), including buses and trucks.

Belt buckle sensors and retractor webbing-extraction sensors fall under this Regulation because 'safety-belt is unfastened' may be detected either by buckle engagement or by pulled-out webbing length.
Instrument cluster telltales, display messages and audible chime generators/HMI logic are relevant as the visual and audible warning means.
Vehicle master control switch logic (e.g. EV 'ready to drive' activation) triggers the first level warning, so power-mode/start-button software is relevant.
Vehicle speed signal processing is relevant because second level warning depends on normal operation (forward motion above 10 km/h).
Changes to number of seating positions, warning location, audible warning type or warning strategy create a new vehicle type and may require extension of approval.
Previously covered by UN R16 (09 series); approvals under R174 and R16 09 series are considered technically equivalent, so legacy R16 SBR approvals map onto this Regulation.
